suggestions.include: Remove #include <dpct/...> once no dpct:: symbols remain.
suggestions.macro: Remove DPCT_* macros (e.g. DPCT_CHECK_ERROR, DPCT_PROFILING_ENABLED) and use plain SYCL.
suggestions.device_queue_management: Own an explicit sycl::queue (e.g. created once in main and passed down) instead of dpct::get_current_device()/in_order_queue(); query device info with q.get_device().get_info<sycl::info::device::...>().
suggestions.events_timing: Use sycl::event returned by submit/parallel_for; for timing create the queue with sycl::property::queue::enable_profiling and read event.get_profiling_info<...>().
suggestions.error_handling: SYCL reports errors with exceptions: delete dpct::err0/DPCT_CHECK_ERROR plumbing and wrap the work in try { ... } catch (const sycl::exception&) plus an async_handler on the queue.
suggestions.memory_management: Use sycl::malloc_device/malloc_shared + q.memcpy/q.memset + sycl::free(ptr, q). Replace dpct::constant_memory/global_memory with a plain USM allocation or a kernel argument.

The final source uses a default-selector sycl::queue with enable_profiling, sycl::malloc_shared/sycl::free for unified memory, a 1-D sycl::nd_range<1> parallel_for with a bounds check, profiling-event timing, and exception handling via catch(sycl::exception). Evidence: compile of the current sources succeeded with 0 warnings and no dpct include (add_dpct_include=false). verify PASSED on 1/1 case (n=1048576): max_abs_err 4.77e-07 against atol 1e-6, 0 mismatches. scan_helpers reports 0 dpct helpers in the current sources (checked three times, most recently on iteration 9). benchmark (10 runs, opencl:0 Intel Xeon CPU): median wall time 258 ms, p95 317 ms; this is whole-process time, not kernel time. Caveat: the loop state still shows zero-helpers-on-current=no, even though scan_helpers returns zero on the same source hash (567bedc0d007d05e) that was compiled and verified.
